headline: Nvidia beat and raised after a down day (revenue $115.8bn, +103%; fiscal 2028 growth guided to 75%), pointing futures higher, but the tape it lands on is S&P -1.0%, VIX +38% on five days and power and software still selling.
regime: Tuesday's close set a fragile base: S&P -1.0%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Semis ETF -0.4% and -16.1% on the month, VIX 24.2 (+38% on five days). Inside AI the chip chain held up best (networking +2.2%, compute +1.8%) while power_nuclear (-2.3%, -8.3% on five days), datacenter_neocloud and ai_software (-3.5%) kept selling ahead of the Anthropic IPO. Nvidia's beat-and-raise after the close gives the chip chain a fundamental floor, but the 10-year at 5.1% and talk of further Fed hikes keep the multiple ceiling low.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Powell record fiscal 2026: $710m quarterly orders, $2.7bn backlog (ba448b4f9c93, db4d07824fe5); POWL +9.2% on five days
Vertiv adds 800 VDC systems for AI compute pods and an ATLAS lab for new silicon (bd0a614a472f, 0fcb5a21dc79); MOD +25.9% on five days
Eisman: the real AI risk is local governments slowing data-centre construction, i.e. siting and power, not chips (5974dfb23790)

Against: power_nuclear -2.3% on the day and -8.3% on five days; NuScale -22% to a 52-week low on a late Canadian SMR (f2008a9ac1b7); Thiel swapped all utilities into a chip ETF (c2ea0a7c009e); Vertiv -7% and 50% off its May high (44fb5127936e, d1d5b2e01ebf)
theses.change_note: -2: order books (Powell, Vertiv) keep confirming the constraint, but money rotated back into chips on the Nvidia print and nuclear is breaking down on execution delays.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Nvidia revenue +103% to a record ~$116bn quarter and fiscal 2028 growth raised to 75% on the Rubin ramp (4c31f8df1c05, 0aee2f823527, 1fe125e227b4)
SpaceX $40bn AI compute bet financed by Goldman and Apollo (28431a1614e1); Huang says he 'could just give all this capacity to Elon' (182f8c500c41)
Networking +2.2% and compute +1.8% on the day; Dell and Coherent rallied on the print (6fb091d2c7b1)
Against: Nvidia ends licensed Hopper sales to China (ce1ea0b459ee) and assumes no China data-centre revenue in its outlook
theses.change_note: +5: the single most important demand datapoint came in well above expectations with a higher forward guide.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Situational Awareness dumped CoreWeave as its book shrank to $1.6bn (fbadea3b28d4); Huang's 'give it all to Elon' remark is bad news for CoreWeave (182f8c500c41)
NBIS -20.9% on five days; MARA AI leases could slip into next year (fecf490b688a); quality gate still drops CRWV, NBIS, IREN, CORZ, CIFR, WULF, APLD
Against: Nvidia calls neoclouds its 'biggest sustained bet' and will keep financing them, 'disciplined' (4b1560d014f5); Blackstone's $5bn AWS DC deal lifts Cipher (1be077d40f53)
theses.change_note: -3: Nvidia explicitly committing to keep funding the ecosystem lowers near-term refinancing risk, though 'disciplined' and the Elon remark say that support is selective.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: SK hynix at a 52-week low, 38% off its September high, still called 'ridiculously cheap' (65514c937512); Nvidia's 75% growth guide implies more HBM
Against: segment -26.6% on the month; DRAM price-fixing suit against MU, Samsung and SK hynix survives dismissal (618c2bf03846); ETFs net sellers of SNDK (8fcc9f9c8830)
theses.change_note: -1: the Nvidia guide helps the demand side, but a live price-fixing case is a new overhang and price action still gives no confirmation; largely a carry-forward.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Blackstone REIT buys 75% of 13 AWS buildings for ~$5bn (1be077d40f53), the second Amazon sale-leaseback signal in two days
Oracle -10% on the month and still fails the quality gate (5712e8bf9c35); hyperscalers -1.6% on the day, -3.7% on five
Against: Microsoft raised its dividend (fd6324b20b43), a sign cash flow still covers payouts
theses.change_note: +2: the AWS deal size confirms hyperscalers are recycling data-centre assets to fund capex.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: S&P -1.0% into the print and below its 200-day (30a9b3bf61b5); VIX +38% on five days; JPMorgan expects more volatility after the beat (e6aff7aa5ca6)
Fed seen tightening further (5a0e5acd4245, 1ba892926891); 10-year 5.1%; Eisman puts AI-bust recession odds at 30% (bf5aa3445638)
Software sold off into the Anthropic IPO, CRM worst (df5de910c92b); ai_software -21.8% on the month
Against: Nvidia at ~20x with doubled earnings undercuts the bubble case for the leaders
theses.change_note: -3: the earnings justification for the leaders got much stronger; crowding and rates still dominate until the tape confirms the print.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Eisman: local governments slowing data-centre construction is the biggest AI risk (5974dfb23790)
House Democrats probe Lutnick over Cantor's Nvidia losses (69abe3766ef1); Vistra faces regulator scrutiny on DC deals (9309bf1a10e4)
theses.change_note: Fresh commentary and a congressional probe, but still no concrete siting or rate action; confidence held.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: Board shot down Huang's offer to return (d751570c4c26); former sales chief tied to customers in the spy scandal (6b2b8764e2dc)
Nvidia ends licensed Hopper shipments to China (ce1ea0b459ee)
Against: the company delivered a record quarter and raised guidance without its founder (4c31f8df1c05, 0aee2f823527)
theses.change_note: -8: the business did not miss a beat under the interim CEO, so key-person risk is now mostly governance headlines; China exit is a known, sized loss.

compute.note: +1.8% on the day after Nvidia's beat-and-raise; AVGO +2.9% on five days, NVDA still -8.0%.

foundry_equipment.note: -0.1% on the day; TSM -9.3% on five days despite the Rubin ramp.

memory_storage.note: -26.6% on the month; cheap but a DRAM price-fixing suit survives.

networking_optical.note: Best on the day at +2.2%; optical called the next bottleneck, ALAB adds Hyve.

servers.note: -1.2% on the day, SMCI -13.1% on five days; HPE and JBL cheap at ~10x but margins thin.

power_nuclear.note: -8.3% on five days, SMR -21.6%; keep weight in cash-generative IPPs, not SMR hopes.

cooling_thermal.note: +6.3% on five days with MOD +25.9%; Vertiv weak on its own news.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -7.0% on five days; Nvidia backing helps but SA fund exited CoreWeave.

hyperscalers.note: -1.6%; Amazon sells AWS buildings to Blackstone to fund capex.

ai_software.note: Worst on the day at -3.5% as the Anthropic IPO pulls money from incumbents.

risks: If Nvidia's beat fades by the close and the Anthropic IPO stumbles, sellers stay in control into year-end.
Further Fed hikes with a 5.1% 10-year cap multiples even as AI earnings rise.
Nuclear execution delays (Canadian SMR late and over budget) spill into power-segment valuations.
Local opposition to data-centre siting slows the build-out that underpins the bottleneck trade.
Neocloud financing depends on Nvidia's 'disciplined' support; any pullback hits CoreWeave and peers first.
watch: Anthropic IPO pricing and first-day trade, and whether software keeps bleeding.
Whether compute and networking hold today's gains or the Semis ETF resumes falling.
Power_nuclear after -8.3% on five days: does CEG's relative strength spread to VST and TLN?
10-year vs 5.1% and any Warsh comment on further hikes.
Sandisk's split on Nov 19 and memory's reaction to the price-fixing suit.
